head: 056341c30d15157d941566c90193c9d384b51d45
public_api: Top-level reexports retain config module as canonical path.
implemented: Strict schema1 JSON, nonzero current broker UID, fixed endpoint/PKI name/server alias/device key.
1..16 distinct typed server pool and principal allowlists constrained to pool; existing bounded pin policy reused.
Root-owned public config/DER and all protected parents, private root-or-broker0600 key, regular/nlink1/size/path bounds.
Pre-open metadata and NOFOLLOW/CLOEXEC/NONBLOCK, fstat identity, max+1 reads, post-read FD/path/parent rechecks; static context/error kind only.
Synchronous bounded-input file/crypto loading; root CLI must offload through owned spawn_blocking. No listener, USB/helper action or override API.
Nine meaningful file/policy tests authored; fixture owner and fixture trust root are explicitly injected only through private cfg(test) context. Production validates actual root chain and UID.
static_checks: Explicit single-file rustfmt2024 with skip_children=true passed; no formatting of other agents files.
git diff --check on owned tracked files passed.
No unsafe blocks, unwrap(), expect() or panic! in owned production/config test source.
not_run: No credential-file positive test with actual root-owned production hierarchy; fixture tests await root execution
No end-to-end TLS USB or helper role evidence from this module
remaining_integration_boundaries: Root must execute compiler/tests and update lock/inventory; backend namespace check remains CLI responsibility.
Helper dedicated broker/secure pool versus legacy pool isolation is a separate authoritative OS role check, not conferred by LoadedConfig fields.
Same service UID is one trusted domain; no claimed same-UID executable isolation or FD revocation.
Multiple credential files are not atomically reloaded; controlled stop/restart required.
Filesystem/crypto calls can block in kernel/synchronous code despite input bounds; no hard wall-clock guarantee.
Native and Rust authenticated catalog/import/long-URB and actual IPv4/IPv6/PCAP acceptance still require integration tests.
